item.title: Ollama
item.description: Runs LLMs locally, exposing them through a simple API (and to any compatible frontend). ollama.com Setup Stack config: github.com/one137/dockerhost-stacks/blob/main/stacks/50-ollama.yml CPU-only inference on the 7945HX, so the container is given generous limits (10G RAM, 22 CPUs) while staying otherwise locked down (read_only, cap_drop: ALL + SYS_NICE, no-new-privileges).

item.title: Clipse API
item.description: Tiny custom API to push clipboard entries to the homelab from anywhere (mainly from iOS shortcuts), and read the latest one back. Entries are written to clipse’s history file, which lives in a Syncthing-synced folder, so anything sent to the API ends up in the clipboard history of my machines.

item.title: Dufs
item.description: Minimal static file server with upload, delete, search and WebDAV support. Handy to share files over http(s) without setting up a share. github.com/sigoden/dufs Setup Stack config: github.com/one137/dockerhost-stacks/blob/main/stacks/50-dufs.yml Files are served from /srv/docker/volumes/dufs/data.

item.title: Network Shares
item.description: TrueNAS iSCSI SMB In TrueNAS Datasets: Add dataset Dataset Preset: SMB (Add to Proxmox) DC, Storage, Add, SMB/CIFS ID: e.g. truenas-proxmox Can check all content types Username “USER” / Password: TrueNAS’s “USER” user account On target system sudo apt install cifs-utils sudo mkdir /etc/samba/ sudo vim /etc/samba/truenas-sambaguest ### username=sambaguest password=*** ### sudo chmod 600 /etc/samba/truenas-sambaguest sudo mkdir /mnt/video-nas sudo vim /etc/fstab ### Add lines //truenas/video /mnt/video-nas cifs credentials=/etc/samba/truenas-sambaguest,uid=1001,gid=1001,file_mode=0664,dir_mode=0775,x-systemd.automount 0 0 ### sudo mount /mnt/video-nas/ # to test If target system is a Synology NAS UI > File Station > Tools > Mount remote folder > CIFS Time Machine over SMB in TrueNAS In TrueNAS: System > SMB > Edit > Advanced > Enable Apple SMB2/3 Protocol Extensions Shares > SMB > (create or edit desired share) > Purpose = Multi-user time machine In macOS: Connect to the share (Finder > Cmd-K) Go to Settings > Time Machine to add the share WebDAV On arch, an easy to use WebDAV shares is with package gvfs-dnssd (“Virtual filesystem implementation for GIO - DNS-SD and WebDAV backend”).
